### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/tenancy/platform-object-tenancy.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/tenancy/system-write-organization.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/tenancy/platform-object-tenancy.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/tenancy/system-write-organization.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 913fd6df8a2b3ec82612bf35dc40f4e062c3077f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9e57470d9ca98cc30657fcce1b1ca880b357417c` — the merge of head `327ad89907d48b1a7d9490e4f16710ad02738610` into base `913fd6df8a2b3ec82612bf35dc40f4e062c3077f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9e57470d9ca98cc30657fcce1b1ca880b357417c && git checkout 9e57470d9ca98cc30657fcce1b1ca880b357417c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 913fd6df8a2b3ec82612bf35dc40f4e062c3077f 327ad89907d48b1a7d9490e4f16710ad02738610 && git checkout -B drift-repro 913fd6df8a2b3ec82612bf35dc40f4e062c3077f && git merge --no-ff 327ad89907d48b1a7d9490e4f16710ad02738610

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 913fd6df8a2b3ec82612bf35dc40f4e062c3077f
```

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The lift under `single`.**
- The diff's only behavioural hunk is `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:7187`: the exemption's early return `isPlatformObjectOutOfTenantAuditScope(object)` is now conjoined with `this.resolveEnginePosture() !== 'single'`. Under `single` an un-admitted platform object falls through to the chain every application object already takes: federated → out; no tenant column (`resolveTenantFieldName`) → out; every row already carrying the column → out; otherwise `resolveSystemWriteOrganization` (`packages/core/src/security/system-write-organization.ts:108`, unchanged): one organization → `derived`, threaded as `DriverOptions.tenantId` at `engine.ts:16030–16047` so the driver's `injectTenantOnInsert` stamps the column; zero organizations with `sys_organization` registered → refuse `no-organization`; two or more → refuse `ambiguous-organization`. The refusal is `SystemWriteOrganizationRequiredError` (code `ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`, `status = 500`, `reason`, `organizationCount`; `tenancy/system-write-organization.ts:329–358`), thrown before driver dispatch, so nothing is written. I re-derived the population from `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json` (44 in reach) and the ledger at head (9 `tenant-scoped` entries, `platform-object-tenancy.ts:145–253`): 35 newly reached, as the PR says. Every one of them reaches D9's one decision.
- The non-refusing paths that remain under `single` are all by construction, pre-existing, and not an exemption: (i) a context or row that carries an organization; (ii) no tenant column, federated, or `tenancy.enabled: false`; (iii) `no-organization-object` (`engine.ts:7203–7215`), a composition that registers no `sys_organization` at all, where the row lands NULL as before. (iii) is D9's own carve-out ("in a composition that registers the organization object"), unchanged by 8b and outside the ruled population (the ruling names the Default Organization, which such a composition cannot hold). No silent NULL path remains on a `single` install that mounts the auth plugin.
- Posture read: `resolveEnginePosture()` (`engine.ts:7039–7047`) reads the injected provider first. That provider is the one plugin-security hands over with `setTenancyPostureProvider`, an accessor returning `this.tenancyPosture` (`security-plugin.ts:1935–1936`), and `this.tenancyPosture` is `normalizeTenancyPosture(tenancy.posture)` from the `tenancy` service (`:1916–1919`): the posture IN FORCE, a degraded wall resolving to `single` there. `AuthPlugin.start()` decides whether to create the Default Organization on the same service's `posture` (`auth-plugin.ts:840`), so the stamping side and the owner-creating side cannot disagree. Without a provider (a lean embedding with no SecurityPlugin) the engine reads `resolveTenancyPosture()` from `@objectstack/types` (`env.ts:147`: `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE`, else `OS_MULTI_ORG_ENABLED`), what the operator asked for. Same reading as the runtime: yes.
- Unresolvable posture: `resolveTenancyPosture()` throws on an unrecognised `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE`; the engine catches and reads `'isolated'` (`engine.ts:7044–7046`, documented at `:7033–7038`). Under 8b that lands on the walled branch: an admitted object is refused (`walled-posture`), an un-admitted platform object keeps the exemption and lands NULL, which is exactly its pre-8b behaviour, so no regression, and fail-toward-isolation is the right direction (guessing `single` would be the worse error). The branch is reachable only by an embedding that bypasses the CLI, since 18.0's operator boot path refuses an invalid posture (`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:6203`). Acceptable; recorded.
- Cost, non-blocking: the posture read now precedes the federated and tenant-field checks for every platform-namespace object, including ones with no tenant column. It is a provider call or an env read, never a query; the "never probes `sys_organization` for a write it does not judge" pin still holds (the walled branch refuses before probing).

**(b) The walled branch.**
- Under `group` / `isolated` the predicate and the return at `engine.ts:7187` are the same expression as before (`isPlatformObjectOutOfTenantAuditScope(object)` → `return undefined`). `PLATFORM_OBJECT_TENANCY`, its 9 entries, `classifyPlatformObjectTenancy` and `isPlatformObjectOutOfTenantAuditScope` are byte-unchanged (that file's diff is docblock only), and the core decision function's walled arm (`posture !== 'single'` → `walled-posture` refusal for an admitted object) is unchanged. Today's exemption is kept exactly, under the walled postures only.
- It is a named posture condition, with the comment citing epic ruling record 6259899486 item 4 and the "never re-narrow it with a per-table list" warning (`engine.ts:7176–7186`). Not a per-table list.
- No walled path changes behaviour. The pins hold the control: `system-write-organization.test.ts` (`isolated` / `group` → `tenantId` undefined) and `tenancy-by-object-classification.test.ts` (`isolated` / `group` un-admitted → undefined; admitted → refused). The `single` control that moved in `system-write-organization.test.ts` (`['isolated','single']` → `['isolated','group']` plus a separate `single` DERIVES case) is the ruled rewrite, not a weakening.

**(c) Boot order: a fresh `single` install boots.**
- `AuthPlugin.start()` calls `ensureDefaultOrganizationExists` under `single` (`auth-plugin.ts:840–857`); a failure throws and fails the boot. Its own writes cannot be refused: `sys_organization` is out of reach (`managedBy: 'better-auth'`, no injected column; census `reach: out`), and the owner bind's `sys_member` row carries `organization_id: defaultOrgId` (`ensure-default-organization.ts:610`).
- Every boot-time producer into the 35 that I could find runs at `kernel:ready`, which the kernel fires only after every plugin's `start()` (`kernel.ts:560–606`, Phase 2 then Phase 3): plugin-webhooks' `bootstrapDeclaredWebhooks` → `sys_webhook` (`webhook-outbox-plugin.ts:223–229`; SYSTEM_CTX insert at `bootstrap-declared-webhooks.ts:256`; failures warn-swallowed at `:323`), plugin-security's platform-admin bootstrap and org-admin backfill (`security-plugin.ts:4534`, `:4685`), service-settings' engine bind (`settings-service-plugin.ts:177`). plugin-email (`email-plugin.ts:498`) and service-messaging (`messaging-service-plugin.ts:316–404`) write no `sys_email_template` / `sys_notification_template` row at boot (no such insert in their src). plugin-security's `start()` writes nothing to an in-reach object: `sys_position`, `sys_permission_set`, `sys_capability` are not among the census's 44. AppPlugin seeds run after plugin-auth (every AppPlugin names it in `optionalDependencies`; topological order at `kernel.ts:1088–1094`), and the seed loader stamps `sys_` / `cloud_` / `ai_` seeds with its sole-organization `fallbackOrgId` through the engine (`seed-loader.ts:488–716`, `:1312–1318`), so #14570's seed-replay row was already stamped by C1.
- First-user sign-up: `settleSelfRegistrationGrant` → `landSelfRegistrationGrant` inserts `sys_user_permission_set` with the first membership's `organization_id` (8b-0f, `auth-manager.ts:5681–5702`); better-auth's `sys_member` / `sys_invitation` rows carry their organization by shape. Sign-up cannot precede `start()`, since `kernel:listening` follows every `start()`.
- So the report's "no producer writes before the Default Organization exists" holds on the code read, and the new dogfood pin measures it on the real showcase composition: it walks every registered platform object with a tenant column (`resolveTenantFieldName` on the registered schema), asks each for `organization_id IS NULL` rows, and floors non-vacuity on objects visited (`inScope` above 30; 44 expected). Caveat, non-blocking: the floor is on objects, not rows, so a producer whose insert was refused and swallowed (the webhook seeder's `catch` only warns) would leave 0 rows and 0 NULL rows and pass. That cannot occur at `kernel:ready` under `single` with the auth plugin mounted, because the organization exists by then; a stronger pin would also assert `sys_webhook` holds a row when the composition declares one. Follow-up material, not a blocker.
- Residual, named for the record: a `single` composition that registers `sys_organization` but mounts no AuthPlugin (an IdentityObjectsPlugin-only or test composition) now REFUSES `no-organization` on every organization-less system insert into the 35. That is the class of about 50 test rigs this PR fixed, it is D9-correct, and the repo ships no production composition of that shape.

**(d) Out-of-scope finding 2: a non-system, organization-less write into a platform object.**
- Factually right: `resolveSystemInsertOrganization` runs for every insert (`engine.ts:16030`) and gates on `carriesOrganization(execCtx?.tenantId)` only (`:7175`), never on `isSystem`. That reach predates 8b (#8844: application objects and the 9 admitted objects already take it for any organization-less context). The exemption 8b lifted was itself context-agnostic, so the population that moved is "an organization-less insert into one of the 35", system or not.
- Inside the ruled scope. D9's text is "every writer"; D11 says `single` is never a reason for a row to be org-less; 6259899486 item 4 names the mechanism (`resolveSystemWriteOrganization`), whose reach is context-agnostic, and its "every system insert" describes the population the seat measured, not a restriction to `isSystem`. Carving `isSystem` out would have needed NEW code (a context check) that re-creates a NULL path D11 forbids. Not an unruled widening; the seat's stage record should carry it explicitly.
- Can a real request path hit the REFUSAL? Only at zero or two-plus organizations under `single`. Zero is impossible after a `single` boot with the auth plugin. Two-plus under `single` is the ambiguous topology the auth plugin already warns about at boot (`auth-plugin.ts:850–855`) and that every application-object write already refuses (#8844); a second organization created at runtime under `single` now also makes the 35 refuse, which the new dogfood pin asserts on purpose. With exactly one organization an anonymous or public door, a guest, a job or cron context (`isSystem`) and a webhook receiver all STAMP, never refuse; the dogfood HTTP doors were green throughout, and real sessions carry the Default Organization through `autoActiveOrganization`. Not a blocker.

**(e) `PLATFORM_OBJECT_TENANCY` kept.**
- Sound. Two readers remain: the walled branch (`engine.ts:7187`) and `buildDriverOptions`' `bypassTenantAudit` mute (`engine.ts:6896–6945`). The mute's only effect is the early return in `auditMissingTenant` (`sql-driver.ts:15683`): one WARN line, nothing a write touches. The ledger header now states both readers and warns against adding an entry to make a `single` write behave (`platform-object-tenancy.ts:6–25`); `system-write-organization.ts`'s docblocks are rewritten to the walled-only reading (`:74–78`, `:90–92`, `:163–164`); `index.ts:557–560` stays accurate (the ledger exists and is exported). The census tooling, its JSON and `lint.yml` are untouched, as claimed. Honestly documented.
- D13 still names the ledger and `isPlatformObjectOutOfTenantAuditScope` for retirement; "retires with its walled reader in 18.x" is consistent with 6259698357 item 3 and 6259899486 item 4.

**(f) Tests.**
- Sampled in full: the two objectql pins, the new dogfood pin, the 8c-T-α commit (`5d1b91e9b`: 4 files, ±5 lines, grant rows stamped with the organization their context reads under, as claimed). Sampled by hunk: plugin-security `legacy-catalog-rows.testkit.ts`, `builtin-positions.boot`, `sys-audit-log-row-scope`, `granted-by-writer-provenance`; plugin-auth `sso-register-platform-admin-gate`, `credential-at-rest-posture`, `driver-fault-auth-log-carriers`; dogfood `single-tenant-identity-create`, `showcase-scope-depth`, `write-door-unreadable-is-not-found`, `wall-package-refusal`.
- The fixture rewrites model reality honestly. Organization-less residue (global grants, the retired catalogue bucket, unscoped platform-admin holders, the pre-change ledger, legacy `sys_position` rows) is landed with `getDriver(...).create(...)` and `organization_id: null`, beneath the engine, as rows an older release left; the readers under test still read NULL rows until 8c, so each assertion pins what it pinned. Fixtures that registered bare `sys_organization` / `sys_user` now declare `managedBy: 'better-auth'` as the platform does, and a `single` rig that needs an owner seeds a Default Organization row. Both move the rigs toward production shape.
- Weakened assertions: the whole test patch was scanned. Five `expect(` lines are removed, each one of the pins the PR names as rewritten to the ruled behaviour and each replaced by the ruled assertion (`tenancy-by-object-classification` ×2, `builtin-positions.boot`'s census control, `single-tenant-identity-create`, `wall-package-refusal`'s `grantsOf` argument); two `it(` blocks became `it.each` equivalents; no `.skip`, `.todo` or `xit` added; no test file deleted.
- `showcase-scope-depth*`: the old empty-`where` `findOne` was refused, swallowed, and a second organization minted; under 8b that would make every organization-less insert ambiguous. Asking `tenancy.defaultOrgId()` is the right fix and closes the trap #14570's remainder named.
- Ablation: the mutation (`!== 'single'` → `!== '8b-ablated'`) restores the exemption in every posture; the 5 objectql cases and the 3 dogfood cases that went red are exactly the cases that separate `single` from the wall, and the 17 other dogfood files going green under the mutation is the right control for "8b is their only cause". The dist-marker preflight and the restore evidence (empty `git diff HEAD`, blob hash, marker `--absent`) are the right shape. Credible; not reproduced here.
- Walled dogfood: no walled dogfood file changes a walled expectation. The walled edits are in rigs whose engine ran at the default `single` while simulating a wall only in plugin services (the report's open question 3), and the `wall-*` files' HTTP doors are untouched.
- Cosmetic: `credential-at-rest-posture.test.ts:235–240` has blank lines interleaved inside a comment block. Harmless; tidy on a later touch.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/15212-8b-single-platform-insert-stamped.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': minor`, the launch-window level for a breaking change (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs:58`: "During the launch window we ship breaking changes as `minor`"); `Check Changeset` and `check-changeset-no-major` are green on the head. The body carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with its reason: no key, export, type or error code is removed, renamed or re-shaped; `check-adr-0087-registration` green), a BREAKING heading, Before / Now / Unchanged, and the one-line remedy (carry `organization_id` on the row, or `tenantId` on the context). That is AGENTS.md §3's form; before / now / remedy stands in for FROM → TO because there is no mapping to state.
- `no (narrowing)` is the right arm: the accept-set shrinks (an organization-less system insert into the 35, previously accepted and stored NULL, is now stamped at one organization and refused at zero or several); nothing is added. Only `@objectstack/objectql` changes source; core's decision function is untouched, so no core bump is owed.
- `Part of #15212`: right. 8b is one stage of C8; the card stays open for the 18.x stages (plan amendment 14). The `Part-of PR must not also close its card` check is green.
- `Part of #14570` (not `Closes`): right on the ruled 18.0 scope. #14570's surviving half (6067177531: a bare `isSystem` insert stores NULL in both postures) is fixed under `single` and pinned on the real showcase; under a wall the row still lands NULL in 18.0 because 6259899486 item 4 keeps the exemption there until 18.x. The claim's "Closes #14570 by construction" was written under #24377 item 5's every-posture shape; the dev's deviation to `Part of` is the correct reading of the amendment. If the seat judges that 18.0's boot-path refusal of walled postures makes the walled NULL path unreachable in the release, closing is a seat ruling to record on #14570, not a PR-body change.
- One wording defect in the remedy paragraph, non-blocking but consumer-facing (it ships in CHANGELOG): "a refusal reading `no-organization` means the write ran before it, or in a composition without the auth plugin's identity objects". The second cause is wrong. Without the identity objects `sys_organization` is not registered, the decision is `no-organization-object`, and the row lands with no refusal.
